_about: Pinned latency baseline for NFR-003 of mission shared-package-boundary-cutover-01KQ22DS. The CI gate compares the median of N fresh `spec-kitty next --agent test --mission clean-install-fixture-01KQ22XX --json` runs against this number and fails the build if regression > tolerance_pct.
pre_cutover_methodology: 5 sequential subprocess runs on macOS Darwin 24.6.0, Python 3.14.0, editable-installed CLI in a fresh venv against the bundled clean-install fixture; median of wall-clock per `time.perf_counter()`.
_ci_target_note: CI runs a Python 3.13 clean wheel on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu, while pre_cutover_median_seconds was captured on macOS Python 3.14 editable install. The gate enforces current_median <= ci_target_median_seconds for CI stability; tolerance_pct remains the default for ad-hoc/local comparisons without this field. Recalibrated on 2026-06-02 from 1.000s to 1.050s after required CI measured a 1.019s median, a 19ms overshoot of the prior absolute ceiling. Recalibrated again on 2026-08-18 from 1.050s to 1.600s — operator-adjudicated (#2749): the 1.050s ceiling had been false-redding repeatedly on CI-runner environment variance (measured CI medians drifting to ~1.25-1.35s with single-run spikes to ~1.78s, e.g. run 32075582367 median 1.334s), while the change under this ceiling is genuinely latency-neutral. Verified during PR #3524 landing by holding the interpreter constant and swapping only src: upstream/main median 1.795s vs PR median 1.783s (statistically identical). 1.600s is ~20% headroom over the observed CI median (matching tolerance_pct=20) and still catches a genuine step-change regression.
_known_regression_note: #2749 ADJUDICATED (2026-08-18): the gate's flakiness at the old 1.050s ceiling was resolved by the operator-sanctioned recalibration to 1.600s recorded in _ci_target_note above — the 'deliberate, documented recalibration once #2749 is adjudicated' the prior note reserved. History: as of 2026-07-17 the gate was FLAKY at the 1.050s boundary — with import-neutral changes it measured ~1.25s (FAIL) on one CI run and passed (<1.05s) on the next. The underlying latency floor traces to the doctrine-as-SSOT / step-authority work (#2723 step.yaml single source + step_projection runtime seam on every `next`; #2722); the deeper optimization (caching step projection on the `next` path) remains #2853's territory and is unaffected by the ceiling move.
